hero.subtitle: A practical comparison for teams deciding whether to keep manual spreadsheets or switch to an operational CRM.

pipeline.hostflow: Shared stage flow with clear owners

q1.q: Can spreadsheets still work for early stage teams?
q1.a: They can for very low volume, but coordination overhead grows quickly when pipeline and documents scale.

q2.q: What is the biggest operational gain from CRM migration?
q2.a: Single-source workflow ownership and reminders, which removes hidden blockers from manual tracking.

q3.q: Do we need a long implementation project?
q3.a: No. Teams can start with baseline onboarding and move active work immediately.

seo.title: Recruitment CRM vs ATS Comparison
seo.description: Understand when a recruitment CRM outperforms ATS-only setup for operational pipeline, documents, and team coordination.

hero.title: Recruitment CRM vs ATS
hero.subtitle: Compare where ATS helps and where CRM-driven operations improve execution speed for active recruiting teams.

items.1: Use ATS when application intake and hiring administration are central.
items.2: Use CRM when operational throughput, ownership, and multi-step follow-up are critical.
items.3: Blend both when your process needs operational control and broader HR stack compatibility.

q1.q: Is ATS enough for operational recruiting teams?
q1.a: ATS is strong for application tracking, but daily recruitment operations often need deeper workflow ownership and follow-up tooling.

q2.a: Yes. Many teams use CRM for operations and ATS for broader hiring records, depending on process maturity.

q3.q: What if we start without ATS integration?
q3.a: You can start with CRM-first workflow and add integrations later when process baseline is stable.

problem.title: What this solves
problem.body: Teams lose time when candidate status lives across chats and spreadsheets. HostFlow centralizes stages, ownership, and reminders, so recruiters and managers work from the same source of truth.

items.1: Create or import candidates into the pipeline.
items.2: Assign responsible users and due actions per stage.
items.3: Track bottlenecks and SLA risks in dashboard and reminders.
